Stationary Availability of a Markov Chain

Source: R/04_savail.R
savail.Rd

Compute the stationary probability of being operational for an irreducible finite-state Markov chain.

Usage

savail(x, up)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

up

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid. States are used in their order in x.

Value

A numeric scalar containing the stationary availability.

Details

Equation (49) of Gavrilopoulos, Trevezas, and Votsi (2026) gives $$A_\infty = \pi e_U = \sum_{i\in U}\pi_i,$$ where \(\pi\) is the stationary distribution of the full transition matrix and \(e_U\) is the operational-state indicator vector. This function uses the same stationary solver as stat(). Both this function and vcov_savail() require an irreducible chain, so the stationary distribution is unique. The result does not depend on the initial distribution, although the complete MarkovChain is validated.

Periodic chains are supported. For them, stationary availability need not equal the limit of avail() from an arbitrary initial distribution. Empty and full operational sets give zero and one, respectively.

References

Gavrilopoulos, G., Trevezas, S., and Votsi, I. (2026). Matrix asymptotic calculus for plug-in maximum likelihood estimators in finite Markov chains. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17161. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17161.

See also

stat(), avail(), vcov_savail()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0.4, 0.6), P)
savail(x, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.6
vcov_savail(x, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.72
